comment: The twelve bundled sample proteins (PLAN.md Phase 0, fallback ladder item 4).
Every sequence is DERIVED from an accession at generation time, never pasted here.
'source' is 'pdb' (RCSB polymer entity) or 'uniprot'. 'range' is 1-based inclusive and
is applied after fetching. 'expect_length' is asserted after the range is applied: a
mismatch is a hard failure, not a warning, because a plausible-but-wrong sequence is the
single easiest way to silently ship the wrong protein.

GFP comes from UniProt rather than a PDB entity on purpose: the crystallised constructs collapse the chromophore into a single non-standard CRO residue, which reaches a folding model as X in the middle of the barrel.

proteins.name: Ubiquitin
proteins.listening_note: The beta-grasp fold. Listen for the long-range contacts that pin the sheet against the helix: they are the low notes, and they arrive late.

proteins.name: Green fluorescent protein
proteins.listening_note: Eleven strands closing into a barrel. The staccato sheet figure builds for the whole piece and only resolves when the barrel shuts.
proteins.reference_note: 1EMA is the S65T variant and collapses the Thr-Tyr-Gly chromophore into a single CRO residue, so its entity sequence is 236 long with an X at position 66. The sequence here is the wild-type pre-cyclisation polypeptide from UniProt, which is what a folding model should be given.

proteins.name: Hen egg white lysozyme
proteins.listening_note: A disulfide-pinned core. The four cystine bridges show up as long-range contacts that form early and never break.

proteins.name: Human proinsulin
proteins.listening_note: Small, and mostly connecting peptide. The C-peptide never settles, so a third of the piece stays unresolved on purpose.

proteins.name: Sperm whale myoglobin
proteins.listening_note: Eight helices and almost no sheet. Nearly pure sustained pad: this is what an all-alpha protein sounds like.

proteins.name: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor, 7TM core
proteins.listening_note: Seven long membrane helices. The pad is enormous and the contacts are almost all local: a GPCR is a bundle, not a knot.

proteins.name: Alpha-synuclein
proteins.listening_note: Intrinsically disordered. It never resolves, so it stays a detuned wash for the whole piece. A trained ear can hear a bad prediction, and this is what one sounds like.

proteins.name: Alpha-3D, a de novo three-helix bundle
proteins.listening_note: Designed, not evolved. It folds cleanly and fast, and the music is almost too tidy: no frustration anywhere.

proteins.name: Trp-cage TC5b
proteins.listening_note: Twenty residues, the smallest thing that folds. Over almost before it starts.

proteins.name: Villin headpiece subdomain HP36
proteins.listening_note: One of the fastest folders known. Three short helices arriving almost together.

proteins.name: Protein G B1 domain
proteins.listening_note: The canonical alpha-beta model system: one helix packed on a four-stranded sheet. Pad and staccato in equal measure.

proteins.name: Pin1 WW domain
proteins.listening_note: All beta, three strands, no helix at all. Pure rhythmic figure with nothing sustained underneath it.
